notes.text: But — Notwithstanding thy gross insensibleness, I will deal mercifully with thee. Created - That made thee his people, and that in so miraculous a manner as if he had created thee a second time. Redeemed - From the Egyptians. Called thee - By the name of God's people, which was as proper and peculiar to them, as the name of Israel.

I gave Egypt — This was fulfilled when the king of Assyria, Esar-haddon, who designed to revenge his father's disgrace, upon the Jews, was diverted and directed by God to employ his forces against Egypt, and Ethiopia, and Seba. Seba - The Sabaeans were confederate with the Ethiopians.
Since — From the time that I chose thee for my people, I have had an affection for thee. Men - As I gave up the Egyptians, so I am ready to give up others to save thee, as occasion requires.

For my glory — And therefore I will glorify my power and goodness, and faithfulness in delivering them. Formed - I have not only created them out of nothing, but I have also formed and made them my peculiar people.

glossa.text:
*And now these things.* Above he spoke of the captivity of the Jews who would not believe; now he addresses the primitive Church, which is of the Jews, that they may understand the Creator of their soul and of their body.

*Creating thee, Jacob.* Jacob is the supplanter, Israel the man seeing God. These are the apostles and apostolic men, who both supplanted vices and deserved to see God.

*Through the waters,* etc. ((ID.)) According to the Hebrews: Through the waters the Egyptians, etc., *as far as* these kingdoms too the apostles passed through by preaching, and the Lord everywhere with them.

*I have given a propitiation.* That from thence thou mayest gain for thyself mercy and a crown, by preaching, namely, to the Egyptians, and to the Ethiopians (who are almost the last) and to the Sabaeans: and Saba is a city situated on the borders of Ethiopia: *Their sound has gone forth into all the earth, and unto the ends,* etc.
*From the East. Many shall come from the East and from the West, and shall sit down with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, from all the parts of the world, that is.*

notes.text: Ye — Ye potentates and rulers of the earth. Glory - By an humble and thankful acknowledgment of it.
Give, &c. — The honour which he deserves: own him as the Almighty, and the only true God. Holiness - Or, in his holy and beautiful house.

The waters — Above in the clouds, which are called waters, Gen. i, 7 chap. xviii, 11. The Divine power displays itself in those high places, which are far above the reach of all earthly potentates. Many - Upon the clouds, in which there are vast treasures of water, and upon which God is said to sit or ride, chap. xviii, 10, 11; civ, 3.
Lebanon — A place famous for strong and lofty cedars.

Them — The cedars; which being broken by the thunder, the parts of them are suddenly and violently hurled hither and thither. Sirion - An high mountain beyond Jordan joining to Lebanon. Lebanon and Sirion are said to skip or leap, both here, and chap. cxiv, 4, by a poetical hyperbole.
Kadesh — An eminent wilderness, vast and terrible, and well known to the Israelites, and wherein possibly they had seen, and observed some such effects of thunder.

To calve — Through the terror it causes, which hastens the birth. He names the hinds, because they bring forth their young with difficulty, Job xxxix, 1, 2. Discovereth - Hebrew. maketh bare, of its trees, which it breaks or strips of their leaves. Glory - Having shewed the terrible effects of God's power in other places, he now shews the blessed privilege of God's people, that are praising God in his temple, when the rest of the world are trembling under the tokens of his displeasure.

The flood — The most violent waters, which sometimes fall from the clouds upon the earth. These are fitly mentioned, as being many times the companions of great thunders. And this may be alleged as another reason, why God's people praised him in his temple, because as he sends terrible tempests and thunders, so he also restrains and over-rules them. Sitteth - He doth sit, and will sit as king forever, sending such tempests when it pleaseth him. He praises God for delivering him, and exhorts others to praise him, ver. 1-5. Recollects his former security, and his prayer when in trouble, ver. 6-10. And stirs himself up to thankfulness, ver. 11, 12. A Psalm and song, at the dedication of the house of David. Title of the psalm. Song - A psalm to be sung with the voice to an instrument. David - At the dedication of David's house, which was built, 2 Sam. v, 11, and doubtless was dedicated, as God had commanded.

glossa.text:
*A psalm of David in the consummation.* ((ID.)) The ark brought back from the Philistines, etc., *as far as* that they may offer themselves to such a consummator.

*Bring to the Lord.* ((ID.)) First he admonishes that sacrifices be offered.

 *The sons of rams.* ((AUG.)) Because assault is not wanting, etc., *as far as* and the seventy-two disciples sent to preach are signified.

*The voice of the Lord.* ((CASS.)) The preaching of Christ terrified minds within, which is, that it gave the spirit of fear to the Jews and to the Gentiles.

((GREG.)) This man ascends from the lowest, that is, from the spirit of fear to the spirit of wisdom, etc., *as far as* that is, spiritual understanding: these the Lord shakes.

((HIER.)) As a husbandman a barren land, etc., *as far as* and he will give strength, and will bless the same in eternal peace.

*The voice of the Lord upon the waters,* etc. ((CASS.)) Of the establishing of the Church, where he enumerates the powers of the Holy Ghost with great proclamation.

*Of Libanus.* Libanus is interpreted a whitening. *The cedars of Libanus,* that is, high men lifted up in earthly things, whom God by breaking will crush small, that is, will bring them back from pride to himself through his beloved Son: and this he will crush by the spirit of fortitude, as a unicorn taken is crushed.
*The desert.* ((CASS., AUG.)) The Jewish people, etc., *as far as* whence flows the living water.

*The Lord.* He shews what is done for the Church now established.

*I have given,* he says, *you power to tread down upon serpents.* But as it is unheard of that stags should strike every kind of wild beast with the horn; so that the Apostles, unlettered, should refute all philosophy.

 *A flood.* ((CASS.)) The waters of baptism, which purges the crimes of the world.

notes.text: And the apostles hearing that Samaria — The inhabitants of that country, had received the word of God - By faith, sent Peter and John - He that sends must be either superior, or at least equal, to him that is sent. It follows that the college of the apostles was equal if not superior to Peter.
The Holy Ghost — In his miraculous gifts? Or his sanctifying graces? Probably in both.

glossa.text: *They sent.* Peter joins John to himself, because virginity is acceptable to the Church, and pleases.

*In the name.* It is not to be read thus, *in the name of Jesus only,* as though the other persons were excluded, but thus: *they were only baptized,* etc., that is, not yet confirmed. *Of Jesus.* Yet before, they *credeban* in the Father and in the Holy Spirit, as did the other Jews. Or, the full faith of one person confirms the faith of the Trinity.
*They laid on hands. ((BEDA.))* Philip, who preached the Gospel in Samaria, one of the seven, etc., *as far as* when he delivers the Spirit the Paraclete to the baptized.
*And while they were supposing. ((ID.))* Not only were they thinking, etc., *as far as* they do not believe that he came through a virgin.

*But there shall come.* Therefore I baptize with water, because he comes who will baptize with the Spirit, and it is fitting that a way be prepared for him.

*Whose I am not worthy. ((BEDA.))* I am not worthy to search out the mystery of the incarnation, etc., *as far as* the evangelical preaching, with which the apostles are shod.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
echoes.note: The Samaritans' reception of the Holy Spirit through the apostles' prayer and laying on of hands extends the outpouring of the Spirit 'upon all flesh' programmatic for Acts. Recurrence within Luke-Acts (cited at Pentecost) is strong; here the volume is faint—no direct verbal contact—so the connection is a thematic continuation rather than a fresh allusion.

echoes.text: Yahweh said to Moses, “Take Joshua the son of Nun, a man in whom is the Spirit, and lay your hand on him. Set him before Eleazar the priest, and before all the congregation; and commission him in their sight. You shall give authority to him, that all the congregation of the children of Israel may obey. He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, who shall inquire for him by the judgment of the Urim before Yahweh. At his word they shall go out, and at his […]
echoes.note: The apostles 'laid their hands on them' and they received the Spirit, recalling the commissioning gesture by which Moses laid hands on Spirit-filled Joshua. Thematic coherence (laying on of hands conveying authority and Spirit) is moderate; the rite is widely attested in the Torah, so volume and distinctiveness are low.

places.name: Jerusalem
places.id: The City of David and Old City, on the spurs above the Kidron Valley, c. 50 km from the Mediterranean. Pre-Israelite Jebus; named here as the seat of Adoni-Zedek, leader of the southern coalition.

places.name: Samaria
places.id: The central hill-country region between Galilee (north) and Judea (south), centered on the city of Sebaste / Samaria (Sebastiya) — the old capital of Omri (1 Kgs 16:24) refounded by Herod. Distinct from the city: pin sits in the regional centre.

echoes.text: “But who can endure the day of his coming? And who will stand when he appears? For he is like a refiner’s fire, and like launderer’s soap; and he will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi, and refine them as gold and silver; and they shall offer to Yahweh offerings in righteousness.
echoes.note: The Coming One who baptizes "with the Holy Spirit and fire" and refines/purges directly answers Malachi 3:2-3, where the messenger of the covenant is like a refiner's fire purifying the sons of Levi. The pairing of fire with purgative judgment-and-cleansing gives high Coherence with John's contrast between the mightier one and himself.

echoes.text: “For, behold, the day comes, it burns as a furnace; and all the proud, and all who work wickedness, will be stubble; and the day that comes will burn them up,” says Yahweh of Armies, “that it shall leave them neither root nor branch.
echoes.note: The winnowing fork separating wheat from chaff to be burned with unquenchable fire mirrors Malachi 4:1 (3:19 MT), where the day burns like a furnace and the wicked are stubble. The threshing-floor/chaff-versus-grain judgment and the inextinguishable fire give this strong Volume.

echoes.text: “They shall go out, and look on the dead bodies of the men who have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they will be loathsome to all mankind.”
echoes.note: "Unquenchable fire" (pyr asbeston) echoes Isaiah 66:24, where the fire upon the rebels' corpses is not quenched, the OT locus for everlasting judgment-fire. The precise eschatological-fire vocabulary gives this real Volume within John's threshing-floor oracle.

echoes.text: I have winnowed them with a fan in the gates of the land; I have bereaved them of children, I have destroyed my people; they didn’t return from their ways.
echoes.note: "I have winnowed them with a fan in the gates of the land" (Jeremiah 15:7) supplies the divine-winnowing image of separating people for judgment that underlies John's fan and threshing floor. The agricultural-judgment metaphor (winnow/scatter the unfaithful) gives solid Coherence.

echoes.text: “It will happen afterward, that I will pour out my Spirit on all flesh; and your sons and your daughters will prophesy. Your old men will dream dreams. Your young men will see visions. And also on the servants and on the handmaids in those days, I will pour out my Spirit.
echoes.note: The promise that the Coming One "will baptize you in the Holy Spirit" resonates with Joel's outpouring of the Spirit on all flesh, a text Luke develops at Pentecost. Faint here, foreshadowing the Lukan Spirit theme; low and contested as the immediate image is refining fire.

echoes.text: I will sprinkle clean water on you, and you shall be clean: from all your filthiness, and from all your idols, will I cleanse you. I will also give you a new heart, and I will put a new spirit within you; and I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you a heart of flesh. I will put my Spirit within you, and cause you to walk in my statutes, and you shall keep my ordinances, and do them.
echoes.note: Spirit-baptism that purifies recalls Ezekiel 36:25-27, where God sprinkles clean water and puts a new Spirit within his people. A reinforcing prophetic Spirit-and-cleansing background for the contrast between water and Spirit baptism; low.

echoes.text: Behold, I have made you into a new sharp threshing instrument with teeth. You will thresh the mountains, and beat them small, and will make the hills like chaff. You will winnow them, and the wind will carry them away, and the whirlwind will scatter them. You will rejoice in Yahweh. You will glory in the Holy One of Israel.
echoes.note: Isaiah 41:15-16 makes Israel a threshing sledge that winnows mountains so the wind carries them off, another winnowing-judgment image feeding John's fan and chaff. Faint reinforcing echo within the OT threshing-floor field; low and contested.

lines: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by name.
You are mine, says the Lord.
When you pass through the waters, I will be with you.
You are mine, says the Lord.
A voice came from heaven: You are my beloved.
Come, let us worship. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Feel the water — cold, then warm, running down, the river closing over and opening again.
You are my beloved; with you I am well pleased.
The same voice that thundered over the deep speaks now, gentle, over you.
You are my beloved; with you I am well pleased.
Do not fear; you have been called by name, and the waters cannot sweep you away.
You are my beloved; with you I am well pleased.
Heaven opens; the Spirit descends; and the word over Jesus is the word over you.
You are my beloved; with you I am well pleased!

lines: Called by name, you pass through the waters unafraid.
You are my beloved; with you I am well pleased.
The voice over the deep speaks gently over you.
You are my beloved; with you I am well pleased.
Heaven opens, the Spirit falls, the word is spoken.
You are my beloved. Come, let us worship. Amen.
